cards.explanation: The answer is Passover, friends. The LORD says, "The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time." (Numbers 9:2) Notice the words "appointed time." This feast has a date on the calendar, and it's not a suggestion. Moses, Israel's leader, gets the word straight from the LORD.

The answer is True. The text says, "The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 9:5) It happened in the Wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. Everything, friends. I can't even get my dough chilled on time, and they did EVERYTHING.

The answer is that they are unclean due to a dead body. The text says these men "…were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day." (Numbers 9:6) Nothing in the text says they did anything wrong, and I'm not going to add anything to it. They were stuck, plain and simple.

The men ask why they should be left out of presenting the LORD's offering. They say, "We are unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" (Numbers 9:7) They name the problem up front and then ask the question anyway. I think that took some nerve, and I admire it. They wanted in, friends.

Moses tells them to wait while he finds out what the LORD commands. He says, "Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you…" (Numbers 9:8) He doesn't make up an answer on the spot. I'd have panicked and handed them a cookie. Moses waits for the LORD's word.

The other situation is being away on a journey. The LORD says that anyone "…unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD." (Numbers 9:10) So the men asked about one situation, and the answer covers a second one too. The LORD gave more than they asked for.

The answer is the second month. The LORD says, "Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month." (Numbers 9:11) Same day number, one month later. The men got a real way back in.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes." (Numbers 9:12) They eat the lamb with unleavened bread and bitter herbs (Numbers 9:11), leave none of it until morning and break none of its bones. A later date, but the same rules.

The answer is that he must be cut off from his people. The text says, "…if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people…" (Numbers 9:13) Notice the two conditions: ceremonially clean and not on a journey. It's a serious line, so I'll just say it plainly. The text says he must be cut off.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, "You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land." (Numbers 9:14) A foreigner dwelling among them who wants to observe the Passover to the LORD does it by the Passover statute and its ordinances. One statute for both.
